A_target.statement:
Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an [[Definition:Entire Function|entire function]] which is [[Definition:Bounded Mapping|bounded]].
Then $f$ is [[Definition:Constant Mapping|constant]].

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be [[Definition:Holomorphic Function|holomorphic]] on a neighborhood of $\size {z - z_0} \le R$, with $\size {\map f z} \le \map M R$ there.
Then:
:$\size {\map {f'} {z_0} } \le \dfrac {\map M R} R$

substitutions.M(R) (bound on the disk): a single global bound M (since f is bounded everywhere)

object_map.reformulation: Apply the Cauchy estimate with the global bound M on disks of radius R, then let R grow without bound.

validity_conditions: f entire allows the Cauchy estimate on a disk of any radius R about any z0.
Boundedness gives a single M with |f| <= M on every disk, so |f'(z0)| <= M/R.
Letting R -> infinity forces f'(z0) = 0 for all z0, hence f is constant.
proof_plan:
Fix $z_0 \in \C$.
By [[Cauchy's Inequality]] on the disk of radius $R$:
:$\size {\map {f'} {z_0} } \le \dfrac {\map M R} R$
As $f$ is bounded, $\map M R \le M$ for all $R$.
